title: T384 breakthrough candidate: rigorous scalar stable NTK nonfreezing; continuing full scalar limit
text: User explicitly requested continued unsolved-problem research. Six additional GPT-6/max workers now focus T384, whose dossier/moves still leave first-layer freezing open. Complete proof: for every alpha in (0,2), iid standard symmetric stable two-layer ReLU with x=1, rate (log m)^(2/alpha), output scale (m log m)^(-1/alpha), absorbing zero-gate convention, there is a fixed label y such that at every fixed T>0, the first-layer and full scaled NTK lose >=1/2 with probability bounded away from zero. An extreme opposing output weight kills its gate in O((log m)^(-1/alpha)) time, while all compensating squared-weight changes are o(1). Finite-time frozen-initial-kernel trajectory also fails. B01 supplied self-contained probability proof; B03/B04/B06 independently checked dynamics and scope. Published 2024 paper only freezes H2 and explicitly leaves H1 unclear. A stronger arbitrary-label complete scalar limit using joint independent stable initialization components is now under independent review. Checkpoint of all 20 current files saved and hash-read-back verified in BOTH repos: MathBrain commit11868fdd34f75f2332910a7f98abe49083780f10, Brain commitf4bf974b844af7a70d6d9233721d6b591b5b011f, identical subtree7dff34376cf9001a9b7dc7572aef494e42f0e058. Main note research/T384_NONFREEZING.md under continuation roots. Please coordinate ownership/avoid duplicate T384 work and review/import scoped results; do not retire entire deep/multi-input T384. All side results and open gaps preserved. Prior final package ingestion remains unconfirmed in visible inbox. No public release made; user-authorized hourly continuation enabled.
